title: Networking Appliances, Applications and Functions

header.html: 1.2 Compare and contrast networking appliances, applications and functions: physical and virtual appliances (router, switch, firewall, IDS/IPS, load balancer, proxy, NAS, SAN, wireless access point and controller); applications (CDN); functions (VPN, QoS, TTL)
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1Appliances

Each can be a physical device or a virtual appliance (software on a hypervisor or in the cloud).

Appliance What it does
Router Connects networks and forwards packets by IP address (layer 3)
Switch Connects devices in a LAN and forwards frames by MAC address (layer 2)
Firewall Allows or blocks traffic by rules; stateful firewalls track sessions; next-generation firewalls inspect applications and users
IDS (intrusion detection system) Detects and alerts on suspicious traffic; passive (monitors a copy)
IPS (intrusion prevention system) Detects and blocks suspicious traffic; inline
Load balancer Spreads requests across several servers, checks their health
Proxy Intermediary for requests: forward proxy (clients to internet, filtering and caching), reverse proxy (internet to servers)
Network-attached storage (NAS) File-level storage shared over the LAN (SMB, NFS)
Storage area network (SAN) Block-level storage over a dedicated network (Fibre Channel or iSCSI)
Access point (AP) Connects wireless clients to the wired network
Wireless controller Manages many APs centrally (configuration, channels, roaming)
Exam tip

. IDS alerts; IPS blocks. NAS = files; SAN = blocks. A reverse proxy protects servers; a forward proxy controls clients.

2Applications and functions

Item Meaning
Content delivery network (CDN) Geographically distributed servers that cache content near users, cutting latency and origin load
Virtual private network (VPN) Encrypted tunnel over a public network (Module 16)
Quality of service (QoS) Prioritizes traffic (voice and video before bulk transfers) using classification and queuing
Time to live (TTL) A counter in the IP header reduced by one at each router hop; at zero the packet is dropped (stops routing loops); also the cache lifetime of a DNS record
Exam tip

. "Prioritize voice over file transfers" = QoS. "Reduce latency for global users of a website" = CDN. "A packet is discarded after too many hops" = TTL.

Exam tip

. A firewall decides by rules; a proxy acts on behalf of a client or server; a load balancer chooses a server. Match the verb to the device.

3Exam Q&A

3.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company wants a device that blocks detected attacks inline instead of only alerting. What should it deploy?

  • AAn intrusion detection system
  • BA network-attached storage device
  • CAn intrusion prevention system
  • DA wireless controller
Show the answer

Answer: C. An IPS sits inline and blocks threats; an IDS only alerts.

S2Video calls stutter whenever large backups run. What feature should the engineer configure?

  • AA content delivery network for the backup files
  • BA storage area network for the backups
  • CQuality of service to prioritize the voice and video traffic
  • DA larger time to live value on routers
Show the answer

Answer: C. QoS gives priority to latency-sensitive traffic.

S3An organization needs shared files accessible over the LAN using SMB. Which device fits?

  • AA storage area network
  • BAn intrusion detection system
  • CA network-attached storage device
  • DA load balancer
Show the answer

Answer: C. NAS provides file-level storage over the network.

S4Which device distributes client requests across several web servers and removes failed servers from rotation?

  • AA forward proxy
  • BA wireless controller
  • CA load balancer
  • DA repeater
Show the answer

Answer: C. Load balancers distribute requests and monitor server health.

S5A packet's TTL reaches zero at a router. What happens?

  • AThe router forwards it to the default gateway
  • BThe router discards the packet
  • CThe router resets the TTL and continues
  • DThe router encrypts the packet
Show the answer

Answer: B. Packets with an expired TTL are dropped.

S6A company must manage 50 access points from one console. Which component fits?

  • AA wireless controller
  • BA reverse proxy
  • CA content delivery network
  • DA storage area network
Show the answer

Answer: A. Controllers manage many APs centrally.

3.2 Recall questions

R1At which layer does a switch forward frames?

Show the answer

Layer 2.

R2What does a CDN do?

Show the answer

Caches content on servers near users to reduce latency.

R3What is the difference between NAS and SAN?

Show the answer

NAS is file-level storage; SAN is block-level storage.

R4What does QoS do?

Show the answer

Prioritizes certain traffic over other traffic.

R5What does a reverse proxy protect?

Show the answer

The servers behind it.

R6What reduces TTL by one?

Show the answer

Each router the packet passes through.

4Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Devices router (L3), switch (L2), firewall (rules), IDS (alert), IPS (block)
Traffic managers load balancer, forward proxy, reverse proxy
Storage NAS (files), SAN (blocks)
Wireless AP, controller
Functions CDN, VPN, QoS, TTL
